props.eyebrow: Wedding and event music at a Colorado Springs resort
props.title: Cheyenne Mountain Resort
props.lede: Cheyenne Mountain Resort sits on 217 acres below Cheyenne Mountain, with its own private lake and a golf course, and over 100,000 sq ft of indoor and outdoor event space.

headingText.html: Couples get married on the beach by the lake, and companies come for meetings and retreats with the mountain right there.

props.title: Live music in each Cheyenne Mountain Resort event space
props.lede: Here’s the act we’d pick for each space. Press play to hear it over the photo.

spaces.name: The lake
spaces.facts: The resort’s private lake has a beach for wedding ceremonies, with the ballrooms as the indoor option.
spaces.why: A solo violin to a full string quartet, from the ceremony through dinner.

spaces.name: Centennial Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Centennial Ballroom is about 4,800 sq ft, built with acoustics for live entertainment. It divides into three smaller spaces.
spaces.why: He can start as a duo and grow to a full band over the evening.

spaces.name: Colorado Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Colorado Ballroom has a stone fireplace, and it holds events of up to about 600 guests.
spaces.why: A six-piece band playing 90s and 2000s R&B and hip-hop, for when you want everyone dancing.

spaces.name: Remingtons Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Remingtons Ballroom is about 3,200 sq ft, for events of up to about 300.
spaces.why: The Doobie Brothers, Steely Dan and Hall and Oates, with three voices and a saxophone.
spaces.alt: Remingtons set for a party, with a lounge sofa, round tables and a stone fireplace.

props.title: Planning music at Cheyenne Mountain Resort

rows.text: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space, and the Centennial Ballroom was built with live music in mind.
We plan load-in and setup with the resort’s events team.
A ceremony at the lake is outdoors, so we’ll plan the music with the indoor backup in mind.
Elevations, the resort’s lounge, has had live music some evenings, so we’ll check the schedule around your event.

props.html: Questions to ask the Cheyenne Mountain Resort events team

items.html: Which spaces have an end time for amplified music, and when is it?
Does the hotel’s AV team need to connect or run the band’s sound, and is there a fee for that?
Where do vendors load in, and when can the band set up?
Is there power near where the band will play?
What wording do you need on the certificate of insurance?

props.html: Forward this list to the events team, or send us the answers and we’ll plan around them.
Questions about music at Cheyenne Mountain Resort

items.q: Can we bring our own band to a wedding at Cheyenne Mountain Resort?
items.a: Hotels like Cheyenne Mountain Resort generally let you book your own entertainment, within their rules on insurance, load-in and sound. Your event manager can confirm them for your date, and we send a certificate of insurance with every booking.

items.q: Does the band need the resort’s AV team?
items.a: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space. The resort’s AV team can add anything beyond that, and we’ll work out the details with your event manager.

items.q: Can one act play the ceremony, the cocktail hour and the reception?
items.a: Yes. The same act can move with you from The lake to The Colorado Ballroom, and one booking covers all of it.

items.q: How much does live music add to a wedding at Cheyenne Mountain Resort?
items.a: It depends on the size of the act and how much of the day it covers. Our pricing page has what live music costs in the Colorado market, and we’ll send a quote for your date.
